Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Presentation: 6 days of dysuria with malodorous urine, intermittent midline lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain rated 7/10, and visible blood spots in urine. No fever, no flank/loin pain, no vaginal discharge. Eating/drinking OK.  
- Most likely diagnosis (consistent with DDx): Acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower UTI) – high likelihood given classic symptoms without systemic features.  
- Other considerations from DDx (lower likelihood, discussed for completeness and to guide safety net):  
  - Nephrolithiasis or bladder stone – medium-low likelihood (hematuria and intermittent pain could fit; absence of flank pain reduces probability).  
  - Urethritis (STI-related) – medium-low likelihood (dysuria possible without discharge; no recent sexual risk factors reported).  
- Management initiated: 3-day course of antibiotics prescribed (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented). Advise increased oral fluids (2.5–3 L/day), optional cranberry juice, and OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets. Advised to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature.  
- Safety net: Seek care urgently if pain worsens, fever develops, lower back/loin pain occurs, urinary retention/obstruction symptoms develop, or symptoms fail to improve. If symptoms recur, follow-up for further evaluation.

Management Plan
- Empiric antibiotics for 3 days (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Hydration advice provided; consider cranberry juice and OTC urine alkalinizing sachets.  
- Monitor temperature at home with a thermometer.  
- Prescription sent to requested pharmacy; patient to pick up within about an hour.  
- Follow-up: Not required if symptoms resolve; return if worsening, non-resolution, or recurrence for further assessment.
